newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Fla., says plans new COPs issues.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Fla., says plans new COPs issues.

text.p: Florida's Orange County School Board plans to refund $157 million of lease revenue bonds and to issue about $100 million of new debt, Fred Winterkamp, senior administrator of treasury services said Tuesday.

The refunding will retire "60-30 type" lease revenue bonds, which were issued in 1990 and subsequently ruled to be subject to the Florida intangibles tax. The tax is levied in January on stocks, certain bonds and other financial instruments held by Florida residents.
"That makes a lot of funds reluctant to hold them. They have to track who's got them, who lives in Florida. It's a bookkeeping nightmare," Winterkamp said.
The debt will be reissued as certifictes of participation, which are not subject to the tax. The county will create a COPs master lease for all 12 or so schools financed with the original issue.
"That makes it an extremely strong credit for an investor," Winterkamp said.
Additionally, with the lease revenue bonds refunded, investors who already hold that debt can treat the new COPs as a new issuer.
"Nobody will have exposure to the district," Winterkamp said. "There should be a large market of people who would be interested in that issue."
The deal, expected in the first half of 1997, will also include $100 million of new money debt to build six new schools.
The debt will probably also be issued as certificates of participation, although the district is reviewing options for a bond referendum, Winterkamp said.
The board received proposals from 26 firms earliler this month in response to an RFP for managing underwriters, and was still reviewing the responses.
